newsitem.title: UK: Physical Brent holds strength, paper spreads weaken.
newsitem.headline: Physical Brent holds strength, paper spreads weaken.

text.p: The Dated Brent market clung to its strength on Friday, with a strong price once more paid for an end August cargo, traders said.
The August 28-30 loader was heard to have moved at September -8 cents between the same parties who traded wet Brents at Sept -5 and -7 on Thursday.
Traders speculated buyers and sellers were both boosting swaps plays and they puzzled over which outlets the buyer would find for his purchases.

The morning deal on a quiet market wiped out the effect of Thursday's third wet Brent trade, which was done at -29 cents between a trader and a European refiner, who argued what he paid was a truer reflection of current physical crude economics.
With the IPE September Brent contract expired, forward crude slipped back slightly, with Sep/Oct valued at -0.05/-0.02 and Oct/Nov drifting down from -9 cents overnight to -12 cents.
Short-term swaps also backed off, with next week (Aug 18-22) trading at 20 cents below October, and the two following weeks valued about the same. An Aug 25-29 to Sept 1-5 roll traded at flat.
One Brent cargo was due to turn wet on Friday, traders said.
With much of Europe enjoying the Assumption Day holiday, other North Sea grades were quiet.
Statfjord barrels were on offer at dated +35 cents, marked up to make up ground on alternative grades that would have to be lifted aboard currently expensive freight.
In the Mediterranean a reported deal on Thursday between two traders for Urals loading August 18-20 at around -70 cents was viewed with considerable scepticism.
"On the Urals we are just waiting for the Sept programme to come out next week and prices will come right down," one trader said. "August is finished and there will be plenty of sour."
Early Sept Urals barrels were heard offered at -90 cents.
With the first shipment of Iraqi oil since May leaving the Turkish port of Ceyhan on Friday Kirkuk blend barrels were being quietly fixed in the Med, dealers said.
Premiums to the OSP of around 10-15 cents were discussed but deals were not immediately visible.
West African grades came under pressure with a combo Bonny Light/Medium fixed on Thursday at +38/+16, lower numbers than achieved early in the week.
Dealers complained that a jump in production of Colombian Cusiana had undercut the appeal of Nigerian grades for the U.S. Gulf.
"Qua Iboe has been hit the hardest because there is so much of it in September," one dealer said, pegging the grade at 31 cents above dated Brent.
